scope: Proposition 4.1 (Exact-cut bridges) of the manuscript “A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments” (preprints/A-directional-zero-one-law-for-finite-range-dependent-random-environments-October-5-2026/directional-zero-one-finite-range.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 220 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 010edc479fd82038), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The renewal masses satisfy ūσ 0 = 1, ūσ j = 0 (1 ≤ j < M), ūσ H = ξuσ H−M (H ≥ M). (4.2) For a list of slabs (γ1, . . . , γm) with total width H, its mass under Bσ H is Bσ H(γ1, . . . , γm) = Qm i=1 W(γi) ūσ H . (4.3) In particular, reversing the list order preserves this law; the steps within each word retain their original order. For H ≥ M, concatenating the list gives the raw marked path through its first hit of H, conditioned on Dσ H. Each such path has a unique parsing into slabs. Concatenating any prescribed slab words, or successive bridges of prescribed widths, gives a raw path weight equal to the product of the constituent raw weights.
